1.overview: Paul introduces himself and the gospel of God concerning Jesus Christ, greets the believers in Rome, and explains his desire to visit them and preach the gospel, which reveals God’s righteousness through faith. He argues that God’s wrath is revealed against human ungodliness: although people know God through creation, they reject and dishonor him, and God gives them over to impurity, dishonorable passions, and a depraved mind.

2.overview: Paul warns that those who judge others while practicing the same sins face God’s impartial judgment, which repays each person according to their deeds. He argues that Gentiles’ consciences testify to God’s law, exposes the hypocrisy of those who boast in the law, and defines true circumcision as a matter of the heart by the Spirit.

3.overview: Paul affirms the Jews’ advantage in receiving God’s words, yet argues that Jewish and Greek unfaithfulness cannot overturn God’s faithfulness and that all people are under sin. He explains that God’s righteousness is revealed through faith in Jesus Christ, who redeems and justifies sinners by grace, excluding boasting while upholding the law.

4.overview: Paul argues from Abraham and David that God credits righteousness through faith apart from works, and that Abraham is the father of both circumcised and uncircumcised believers. He traces Abraham’s trust in God’s promise and applies the same principle to those who believe in the God who raised Jesus, delivered over for their trespasses and raised for their justification.

5.overview: Paul says that those justified by faith have peace with God through Jesus Christ, rejoice in hope and suffering, and are assured of salvation because Christ dies for them while they are sinners and enemies. He contrasts Adam’s trespass, which brings sin and death, with Christ’s righteous act and obedience, through which grace brings justification, righteousness, and eternal life, while the law makes trespass increase.

6.overview: Paul argues that those baptized into Christ share in his death and resurrection, so their old selves are freed from sin and alive to God. He contrasts slavery to sin, which leads to death, with slavery to righteousness and God, which leads to holiness and eternal life through Christ.

sections.heading: United with Christ in Death and Life

7.overview: Paul uses the marriage bond to explain that believers die to the law through Christ and belong to the risen Christ, serving in the new way of the Spirit. He argues that the law is holy but sin uses the commandment to bring death, and he describes the struggle between delight in God’s law and sin in the body, giving thanks for rescue through Jesus Christ.

8.overview: Paul declares that those in Christ Jesus are free from condemnation through the Spirit, who gives life, marks them as God’s children, and will raise their mortal bodies. He contrasts present suffering with coming glory, describes creation and believers waiting in hope with the Spirit’s help, and affirms that God’s purpose and Christ’s intercession secure believers against every accusation and separation from God’s love.

sections.heading: God’s Love and the Believers’ Security

9.overview: Paul grieves over Israel and explains that God’s word has not failed: God’s purpose rests on his call and mercy, as shown through Isaac, Jacob, Pharaoh, and the potter’s authority. He cites Hosea and Isaiah concerning Gentiles called as God’s people, Israel’s remnant, and the stone in Zion, concluding that Gentiles attain righteousness by faith while Israel stumbles in pursuing it by works.

sections.heading: God’s purpose in election and mercy
The potter, mercy, and the remnant
Righteousness by faith and the stumbling stone

10.overview: Paul expresses his desire for Israel’s salvation, explaining that Israel’s zeal lacks knowledge of God’s righteousness and that Christ is the end of the law for everyone who believes. He describes salvation through faith in the risen Jesus and the proclamation of the word, then argues that Israel has heard the message but remains disobedient while Gentiles find God.

11.overview: Paul argues that God has preserved a remnant of Israel by grace, while Israel’s trespass brings salvation to the Gentiles. He describes the grafting of Gentiles and the future mercy shown to Israel, then praises the depth of God’s wisdom and the source of all things.

sections.heading: Gentiles Grafted into the Olive Tree

12.overview: Paul urges believers to offer themselves to God, be transformed by renewed minds, and exercise their gifts humbly as members of one body in Christ. He describes sincere love and communal conduct, including blessing persecutors, pursuing peace, and overcoming evil with good.

13.overview: Paul teaches that governing authorities are appointed by God and that submission includes paying what is owed and showing respect. He presents love of neighbor as the fulfillment of the law and urges believers to live decently in view of approaching salvation, putting on the Lord Jesus Christ.

14.overview: Paul addresses disputes over food and sacred days, telling believers not to judge or belittle one another because each belongs to the Lord and will answer to God. He urges them to avoid causing a fellow believer to stumble, emphasizing that God’s kingdom is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit and that each person should act from faith.

sections.heading: Belonging to the Lord and God’s Judgment

15.overview: Paul urges the strong to bear with the weak and calls for unity among Jews and Gentiles, grounding their shared praise in Christ and the Scriptures. He describes his ministry to the Gentiles, plans to travel to Spain after delivering aid to Jerusalem, and asks the Roman believers to pray for his safety and welcome.

sections.heading: Paul’s Travel Plans and Prayer Request

16.overview: Paul commends Phoebe to the Roman church and sends greetings to numerous believers, including Prisca and Aquila, while conveying greetings from other churches and coworkers. He warns against divisive teachers, reports greetings from his companions, and praises God for strengthening believers through the gospel and revealing the mystery of Christ to all nations.
